notes: Defensive pass interference. Defender contacts and restricts receiver before the ball arrives. Common confusion: not holding because the ball is in flight and the receiver is attempting to catch a forward pass.

DPI category: early_contact. Obvious early contact before the ball arrives; defender materially restricts receiver before the pass gets there. Common confusion: not holding because the pass is in flight and the receiver is attempting to catch a forward pass.

DPI category: arm_bar/body_restrict. Borderline DPI. Defender restricts the receiver before the ball arrives on a catchable pass. Common confusion: incidental hand fighting versus restriction that affects the catch opportunity.
No foul. This should not be ruled pass interference. Common confusion: do not call DPI unless the defender materially restricts the receiver before the ball arrives and affects the catch opportunity.
No foul. Some contact occurs, but do not call defensive pass interference without material restriction affecting the catch opportunity.
No foul. No offensive pass interference on the play. Do not call OPI without material offensive restriction/contact that creates an illegal advantage before the pass is touched.

Obvious defensive pass interference. Defender materially restricts the receiver before the ball arrives and affects the catch opportunity. Common confusion: do not call OPI; the defender is responsible for the restriction.

Obvious offensive pass interference. Offensive player materially restricts the defender or creates illegal separation before the pass is touched. Common confusion: legal route contact or incidental hand fighting.
No foul. Offensive pass interference review clip where contact/hand fighting does not materially restrict the defender or create illegal separation before the pass is touched.

Obvious offensive pass interference. Offensive player materially restricts the defender or creates illegal separation before the pass is touched. Common confusion: legal route contact or incidental hand fighting.

Obvious offensive holding. Blocker materially restricts defender outside the frame of the body and affects the play. Common confusion: not a legal block when the defender is grabbed, hooked, turned, or prevented from disengaging.

Obvious offensive holding. Blocker materially restricts defender outside the frame of the body and affects the play. Common confusion: not a legal block when the defender is grabbed, hooked, turned, or prevented from disengaging.

Obvious offensive holding at the point of attack. Blocker materially restricts defender and affects the play. Common confusion: do not ignore as away from the play because the restriction affects the run lane or play direction.

Obvious block in the back. Blocker contacts opponent from behind and above the waist in a way that affects the play. Common confusion: not holding; the key action is forceful contact from behind rather than restraint.

No foul. Borderline holding action, but no call because the contact does not rise to material restriction affecting the play. Common confusion: do not call holding for brief contact, hand placement, or minor jersey contact without meaningful restriction.

No foul. No defensive or offensive pass interference: clean coverage / legal contact with no material restriction by either player. Common confusion: do not call DPI or OPI for incidental contact or normal hand fighting that does not affect the catch opportunity.

No foul. No defensive or offensive pass interference because neither player materially restricts the opponent in a way that affects the catch opportunity. Common confusion: incidental contact, mutual hand fighting, or contact that does not create an advantage is not DPI or OPI.

No foul. No block in the back because the contact does not meet the rule standard for an illegal block in the back or does not materially affect the play. Common confusion: do not call block in the back for legal side contact, incidental contact, or contact that does not create an advantage.
Obvious illegal formation. Offense is improperly aligned at the snap. Common confusion: not illegal motion or illegal shift when the issue is the set formation/alignment at the snap.

No foul. Borderline illegal-motion review clip, but the motion is legal or does not meet the illegal-motion rule standard at the snap. Common confusion: do not call illegal motion unless a player is moving forward at the snap or more than one player is illegally in motion.

No foul. This is not an illegal shift because the movement is legal or does not meet the illegal-shift rule standard before the snap. Common confusion: do not call illegal shift unless the offense shifts and fails to become legally set before the snap.

Personal foul: illegal blindside block. Blocker initiates forceful blindside contact against an opponent. Common confusion: not ordinary legal contact or generic unnecessary roughness; the key is forceful blindside contact.

Personal foul: targeting. Player initiates forcible targeted contact against an opponent. Common confusion: not ordinary contact; the key is forcible targeted contact that meets the personal-foul standard.

Obvious horse-collar tackle. Defender grabs the runner from behind or side and pulls the runner down by the collar/shoulder-pad area. Common confusion: not a legal tackle when the pull-down mechanism fits the horse-collar rule.

Not kick-catch interference. Receiver is not denied an unimpeded opportunity to catch the kick. Common confusion: do not call kick-catch interference unless the receiver's opportunity to catch is materially impeded.
Roughing the kicker. Kicker is contacted after the kick when the defender could have avoided contact. Common confusion: distinguish roughing from running into based on severity and danger.
Obvious free kick out of bounds. Kick goes out of bounds untouched by the receiving team. Common confusion: not kick-catch interference because no receiver catch opportunity is involved.
